questions.title: Where lymph node plasma cells sit
questions.question: Which part of the lymph node contains numerous plasma cells?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cortical sinuses are spaces lined by endothelium and macrophages that separate the cortical follicles from the capsule and trabeculae; they filter lymph rather than housing the numerous plasma cells this question asks about.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Medullary sinuses are the channels between the medullary cords, lined by endothelium and macrophages, that filter lymph on its way to the hilum; the plasma cells sit in the cords beside them, not in the sinuses themselves.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Connective tissue trabeculae are structural septa extending inward from the capsule; they are not a site where plasma cells accumulate.
explanations.D: Correct. The medullary cords, irregular branching cords of B lymphocytes, plasma cells and macrophages in the lymph node's medulla, are where numerous plasma cells are found. These cords may be continuous with the cortical follicles, reflecting the path B lymphocytes take as they differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Primary cortical follicles are aggregates of mainly naive B lymphocytes in the cortex, before antigen-driven activation; they are not where the numerous, already-differentiated plasma cells of the medulla are found.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the medullary cords as the lymph node compartment where numerous plasma cells are found.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter beside option, p.28

questions.title: Where lymphoid follicles are found in the lymph node
questions.question: In the lymph node, the lymphoid follicles are found in:

explanations.A: Correct. Lymphoid follicles are found in the outer part of the lymph node's cortex. Primary follicles there are mainly B lymphocytes. Once antigen has driven activation, some become secondary follicles with a pale germinal centre surrounded by a darker rim of small lymphocytes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The medulla holds medullary cords and sinuses, not lymphoid follicles, which are a cortical structure.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The paracortex, between the cortex and medulla, is the thymus-dependent zone of T lymphocytes only; it specifically has no follicle and no germinal centre of its own.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Red pulp is a compartment of the spleen, not the lymph node; the two organs' terminology should not be mixed.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The connective tissue trabeculae are structural septa extending in from the capsule, not the site of the lymphoid follicles, which sit in the cortex between them.

questions.learning_objective: State that lymphoid follicles sit in the lymph node's cortex, as distinct from the paracortex's T-lymphocyte-only zone and the medulla's cords and sinuses.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter beside option, p.28

questions.title: The encapsulated lymphatic organ
questions.question: Which of the following is an encapsulated lymphatic organ?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diffuse lymphatic tissue is scattered lymphocytes within a connective tissue framework without a distinct capsule of its own.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lymph follicles are aggregates of lymphocytes found within various organs (lymph node, spleen, tonsil); a follicle itself has no independent capsule.
explanations.C: Correct. The lymph node is a discrete, encapsulated lymphatic organ. A dense connective tissue capsule surrounds it, sending trabeculae inward. That capsule is what lets it be identified as an individual organ, with its own afferent and efferent lymphatic vessels, rather than diffuse tissue scattered within another organ.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Peyer's patches are aggregates of lymphoid follicles in the wall of the ileum; they are part of the gut wall, not a separately encapsulated organ.
explanations.E: Incorrect. White pulp is a compartment within the spleen, itself encapsulated as a whole organ, but white pulp is not itself a separately capsulated structure.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the lymph node as an encapsulated lymphatic organ, as distinct from diffuse lymphatic tissue, follicles and Peyer's patches.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter beside option, p.28

questions.title: Lymph follicles of the spleen
questions.question: Lymph follicles (lymphatic tissue collections) of the spleen are called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Blood sinusoids are the wide, irregular vascular channels of the red pulp, not the lymphatic tissue collections this question asks about.
explanations.B: Correct. The spleen's lymphatic tissue collections are called white pulp, scattered irregularly throughout the red pulp. White pulp is organised concentrically around a central arteriole and contains the spleen's B- and T-lymphocyte zones, functionally analogous to a lymph node's follicles and paracortex.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Cortical follicles" is lymph-node terminology (the lymph node's cortex holds follicles); the spleen has no cortex/medulla division and its equivalent lymphatic tissue is instead called white pulp.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Red pulp is the spleen's OTHER compartment — Billroth cords and blood sinusoids — not the lymphatic tissue collections asked for here.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Billroth cords are a structural component of the red pulp, between the sinusoids, not the lymphatic tissue collections (white pulp) this question is asking about.

questions.learning_objective: Identify white pulp as the spleen's lymphatic tissue collections, as distinct from the red pulp's Billroth cords and sinusoids.

questions.title: Where Hassall's corpuscles are found (past-exam block, دفعة 63)
questions.question: Hassall's corpuscles are found in which of the following?

options.A: The red pulp of the spleen

explanations.A: Incorrect. The splenic red pulp is Billroth cords and blood sinusoids; it contains no Hassall's corpuscles, which are a thymic, not splenic, structure.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hassall's corpuscles are a thymic structure, not a lymph node one; the lymph node cortex instead holds lymphoid follicles.
explanations.C: Correct. Hassall's corpuscles — concentric epithelial bodies with a degenerating acidophilic centre — are found only in the medulla of the thymus lobule. They are a normal constituent of the thymic medulla at every age and occur nowhere else in the body, so finding one identifies both the organ and the zone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The thymic cortex is densely packed with proliferating T-lymphocyte precursors (thymocytes); Hassall's corpuscles are specifically a medullary, not cortical, feature of the thymus.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Splenic white pulp is lymphatic tissue around a central arteriole; it contains no Hassall's corpuscles, which are exclusive to the thymic medulla.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Hassall's corpuscles as a structure exclusive to the thymic medulla, as distinct from the thymic cortex and from splenic red/white pulp.
